messages.content: The world reforms. Briar's hands deftly maneuver the instrument held within her grip. The violin produces a melody as she plays it just as she was taught by her brother. Kit sits across from her, watching with a gentle expression.
She smiles as him, before closing her eyes completely focused on her movements playing a beautiful melody
Music fills every inch of the room, reverberating back towards its source. In this one moment, nothing else exists beyond Briar's thoughts and her song.
Her smile shines brightly, and her body moves likes she is dancing softly
Eventually, her song reaches its inevitable conclusion, and Kit gives a gentle, but enthusiastic applause, filling the audience of one.
She bowed "Did you enjoy the melody?"
He places a hand over his chest, and speaks in admiration. "It was beautiful, sis. You've truly made your performances your own. It's only a matter of time before your talent is widely recognized."
She jumped excitedly "I'm so glad!"

He looks unsure of what to say for a moment, his expression shifting a few times, before settling on a somber appearance. "In fact, I would go as far to say... you no longer require my instruction. Which leads to a rather... difficult topic."
She tilts her head to the side "What do you mean?"

"...This life here in Bander. I've loved it, sis. It's had its share of problems, but I don't regret a single thing I've done here." He closes his eyes, and sighs. "...but, I don't think I can build the future I'm looking towards here."
"Oh... Are you leaving...?"

He stares out the south-facing window as he speaks. "Yes... to Newark. Yondova is a beautiful nation, but it lacks imagination. I want to build a world where those born into unfortunate lives can live truly free. Yondova has stagnated under incompetent... well, I don't wish to bore you with the details."
She placed her violin on the table and walked to Kit to hug him "I will miss you a lot Kit... But I understand. Do what makes you happy"
"Did you already tell father?"

He returns the hug, holding her tight for a moment before letting go. "Yes. He was rather happy to hear the news. He seems to believe I've been wasting my life these past years... How frustrating, such a double standard..."
She sighed "Father is so annoying but I'm glad he didn't pressure you to stay... I will miss you a lot Kit"

"As will I miss you..." He stands, and gives her a loving smile. "It won't be forever, though. I won't abandon you, sis, trust me on that. I don't know if you need me anymore, but... well, maybe on some level I still need you. I'll visit, or... arrange for you to visit, if necessary. Of course, I will need some time to settle into Newark before I can think about such matters..."
"I will always need you brother, you are the only person I have... You better visit!" she pouted

He smiles at her pouting, a face that should express amusement, but his eyes speak of a deeper sadness at her words. "Yes... of course. I'll be leaving in a few weeks, but I don't want to forget to say, that... I love you, sis. I always will."
She smiles "Always love you too brother!"

The world shifts. Kit has left on pursuit of a brighter future where Briar cannot follow. Her parents are out of the house at the moment, leaving her alone with her only remaining companion. Her violin sits in front of her, ready to play.

Briar grabs it with both her hands and stares at it, taking in every detail. The beautiful wood, the roses she had painted onto it, the white strings. She positioned it on her shoulder and closing her eyes she started playing a new melody. Her music was usually upbeat, her goal was always to bring happiness to others. But now that she was alone, she played a melody filled with melancholy and sadness.

A new sound fills the walls. It follows the contours, pressing itself against every detail and imperfection, just as the songs had before. The house maintains its shape, as does Briar, but the song filling both can no longer be recognized. You can fill a mold with whatever you wish, but to believe its properties remain the same is delusion. On that day, the McGregor twins changed fundamentally. A chemical reaction that could never be undone. A crack that could never be filled. An impurity he could never scrub away.
**End Chapter 10.1**

The world reforms. Mari sits in the comfort of her home, as Emil prepares a meal. Pearl hasn't arrived home from her work yet, providing the house a brief quiet. She's been in something of a mood ever since Azalea Thompson had performed in town a few weeks back.
What's he making?
Spaghetti.
Yeah, that tracks. We end up eating a lot of spaghetti in this house, and yet, somehow, it tastes just as good every time... interesting, isn't it?
"Add some extra cheese to mine, dad. Thanks."
I lean back in my chair, staring up at the ceiling while I wait.

"Mhm." He nods.

As he finishes preparing the meal, the door of the household slams open, followed by stomps towards the dining area.
I slowly lower myself back into a regular sitting position. In all likelihood, she won't notice me, but it's best to be as nothing as possible if she does.

"I can't BELIEVE this! THREE weeks since the concert, and STILL everyone's RAVING about Azalea this, Azalea that. How am I meant to keep their attention!? How could you let this happen!?" Pearl storms in, with an accusatory finger pointed at Emil.

Emil just sighs, and sets the plates. Mari's has extra cheese, as requested.
I twirl the noodles onto my fork and take a bite. It tastes exactly like sand, as always. But I do my best to appreciate the cheese.

She's asking a good question, for once. He probably should have known better than to expect this would turn out any differently. I look up at her, trying not to seem too intrusive. "May I be excused, mom?"

She's surprised for a moment, as if having forgotten Mari was even there, or never noticing her in the first place. She quickly transitions into digging through the wine cabinet as she responds. "No, no! Young lady, you'll eat with your FAMILY. We have proper VALUES here, unlike some two-bit circus acts! Besides, YOU saw her too, didn't you? What about YOU, huh!? Think she outclasses your MOTHER!?"
"I didn't really get a sense of what her values were. Maybe you're right." I look back at the table, resolving myself to a long night.

"Hmph. Of course I am." She just starts drinking straight out of the bottle, and snaps her attention back to Emil. "See!? Is that so HARD!?"

Emil finishes a bite of his food, and gives a weak response. "...It wasn't up to me. I'm not her manager, she's the royal musician. We can't stop her from performing, even if..."

"Even if you WANTED to? Which you DON'T, obviously. Good for BUSINESS, having a youthful, pretty face, huh? We didn't HAVE to attend, DID we!? What do you SEE in her, HONESTLY."

I wonder if Azalea has a husband. I wonder how she treats him, what demands she makes of him. She probably doesn't need many, right? They would just go with the flow... she would come home from a long day of work to a nice meal, and hey, maybe that meal would taste like sand too. But she would appreciate it anyways, because that's the way it always is, because it's what comforts her. Keeps her grounded. That's probably the kind of person she is.
"Any cheese, mom?"
Pearl stares at her daughter, her eyes hazy and unfocused. "...What? Why would I want..." Her eyes wander to the table. "Oh. Spaghetti. Again. Typical."
"Typical," I parrot.

"HONESTLY, Emil. Do you even KNOW how to cook anything else? Hahahaaaa, or is your culinary taste as limited as your musical taste! Afraid to branch out, even a LITTLE?" She doesn't take a seat at the table, instead leaning against the wall.

"I've... tried to pitch you for some gigs, but... well, after the... creative conflicts the last few times, I'm already risking losing my..." He seems to be straining to find words that won't upset her further.
Just stop, dad... please... you're not going to win. There's nothing to win. It's obvious, isn't it? Does he still not get it?
I try again. "Do you want any cheese, mom?"

"Are you a broken RECORD!? I'm not HUNGRY, I don't need your father's CHARITY. Ha! I'll do it on my OWN." She finishes downing the contents of the bottle.

"Honey, you... really should-" Before Emil can finish, something flies past his head. Glass shatters on the wall behind him, as the wine bottle shatters.

"I don't NEED anything from YOU! Or ANYONE in this tone-deaf nation! If you want to give me something, give me a ticket OUT of here."
I recoil, nearly falling out of my seat. "Mom, I...!" I clamp my mouth shut before anything else can come out and upset her even more. I should be used to this by now, too.
She would never have hit him with the bottle. He's not in any danger. I'm not in any danger. It's safe.
I'd say I want that ticket for myself, but it wouldn't be true. Everything I need is here.
Emil slowly looks from the broken bottle, to Pearl, to Mari. He closes his eyes to think for a moment, then motions towards her. "Lammy, why don't you get the dustpan and broom?"
"Mhm." I get up and go to retrieve them. When I'm back, I start sweeping up the glass myself.

His expression portrays disappointment at this, for some reason.

"I'm RIGHT here, why can't they SEE!? What is it ABOUT her, what IS it... I've learned all her songs, bet I can do them BETTER than her, even, ha!" She reaches for another bottle.
"Please don't."
"Don't *what*?" She stares at her daughter with a dizzy expression.
"I just... think you shouldn't... or you'll get a headache tomorrow..." I try to finish the sweeping faster.

Mari successfully finishes sweeping.

"Like it'll even MATTER. No one likes my performance SOBER, huh!? So why's it MATTER. Just made up BULLSHIT, do THIS and THAT, like SHE does any, she's just, she doesn't even... in SOCIETY..." She looks like she's about to collapse.
I hurriedly dump the contents of the dustpan into the trash. It's better that she doesn't collapse onto them. "Um, may I be excused, mom?"
She steadies herself, and takes a seat. She shoves her plate to the side and rests her head in her hands. "WHY do you keep asking!? Calamari, just LEAVE if you want. You're giving me a HEADACHE."
"Thank you." I pick up my plate and fork and bring the pasta to my room, shutting the door behind me before sitting down on my bed.
After a minute or two of unsuccessfully trying to hype myself up to take a second bite of the noodles, I give up and just stare at the door, listening for further conversation.

Screaming, throwing, even some sobbing.

It's so routine, so mundane. Obviously Calamari knows what she's going to hear. She's not listening out of curiosity. Is it a self-punishment, then? Better to flog herself in private rather than onstage. She's always so courteous.

Who says it's not curiosity? Maybe it's not about the generic description. Maybe there are specific words that are being said, certain phrasing choices, that set this apart from all of their other arguments. Maybe there's even something about it, the ways they try to redirect themselves from happiness, that I need to understand. It's sad, of course, but it always tells me something new, it always teaches me something - I need to hear, I need to listen. I need to figure out the pattern, the subtle cues they give each other, I just... it's not punishment, it's not courtesy. It just is what it is.
I've done enough listening for tonight, though. I think I got it.
May I go to bed?

A sad little girl pretends that she doesn't understand. That she doesn't understand she's already gone to bed. That she doesn't understand that misery is inherent to human nature. That she doesn't understand her mother is moments away from clawing out her husband's throat. That she doesn't understand her mother would be correct to do so. That she doesn't understand how freeing it would be to return the favor.
**End Chapter 10.1**

The world reforms. Atie is in attendance of a lecture for her engineering studies. The professor drones on over today's lesson, as several students stare with confusion, desperately copying notes. However, one student on the other side of the classroom stares with clarity and intensity. Atie's seen her a few times, but hasn't spoken to her yet.
[That girl looks quite interested. Or maybe she's struggling to pass... I wouldn't know.]

"That concludes the history of springlock mechanisms. You are now dismissed. Your final essays will be due shortly, keep that in mind during your private studies." The professor gets to clearing his blackboard as the students stand up, gathering their items.
Atie gathers her things slowly while looking around, waiting for more people to get out so it's a little less crowded.
A majority of the students begin to shuffle out, but a handful stay behind, gathering around the girl with the intense gaze. She seems to be rather popular, and gets to chatting with them.
Atie notices them and gets distracted, wondering if all of those people are talking to her.
The girl seems to notice Atie in return, and the two meet gazes for a moment. She quickly looks away and returns to her conversation.
[She caught me looking... I should be going home anyway...]
As Atie thinks this, the girl appears to wrap up her conversation. The rest of her posse leaves ahead of her, as she begins to walk straight towards Atie.
"Hiya!" She waves. "I don't believe we've ever spoken. I'm Penny. Penny Welsh."

It was pretty sudden. Atie has not spoken in a while, and her voice fails.
"h--  Hello..."

Penny nods, and confidently moves the conversation forward. "I was wondering if you'd like to join us for a study group sometime? We're getting into some pretty complex material, and it helps a lot more than you'd think. No pressure, of course."
Atie is still stunned by the sudden conversation. "Oh, uh... Sure. Yeah. Um, why not pressure? Isn't that important for springlocks?"
"Pffttthaahaha, I guess it is!" She covers her mouth as she laughs. "Alright, pressure it is, then. You free tomorrow?"

The laugh flusters her a little more. She takes several seconds to get past it and respond.
"Yeah."
"So... Got a name?" She cocks her head to the side a bit. "Sorry, just... usually that's how conversations start."
"Atie."
"Alright, see you later, Atie!" She gives another wave, and exits the classroom.
"Bye...!" Atie waves back.
Atie is alone.
Atie thinks about it and imagines what the study group might be like, before regaining her senses and getting up.
As Atie stands, the weight of her body proves too much for her legs. She collapses, falling to her knees. Upon impact with the floor, her legs crack, beginning to break up into small particles.
The cracks spread through her legs, and the thousands of tiny pieces of Atie begin to seep into the ground, no longer bound to the shape of her body.
Atie feels powerless to do anything.

A man steps through the doors of the classroom. White robes trail behind him as he steps towards Atie.

"You're not done here. Not yet."
"Why?"
He grabs Atie's hair, and drags her across the floor. The cracks reach her torso, leaving a trail of tiny fragments of Atie along the ground behind her.
Atie feels like crying, but can't tell if she already is.

Her tear ducts crack. They're not hers to use. None of her body is.

"She was such a cheerful girl. I wonder what happened? What broke her? Some people are just cursed. To no fault of their own, everyone around them is hurt. I don't think that's true for Penelope."
Atie closes her eyes.

Atie can feel it reach her neck. There's so little of her left.

"I think she loves the pain. She wants it because it wasn't hers. She sees others suffering and it makes her jealous. How utterly selfish, to throw away a perfect life out of this fetishized perception. She's wrong, though. You haven't felt pain even a single day in your life, have you?"
Atie waits.

"No, you just trample over us. You don't even realize you're doing it. That's the worst part. You have no idea how much had to be sacrificed for you worker drones. Well, go ahead, build the future. I won't stop you from overturning a grave. Just don't blame me when it needs a new occupant."

He lets go of her hair, dropping her head to the ground. It shatters, spreading across the floor, and rolling into its imperceptible crevices. Pieces of Atie tumble through the ground, tunneling several stories down through loose soil, before ultimately bursting through a stone wall. Particles of her lay in a heap on the cold, hard floor.
Atie waits.

She begins to pull herself together, as if her body is magnetically drawn to its latest orientation. Her eyes are the first to be pieced together. With no eyelids, she's unable to shut them. She's in a hallway carved out of sandstone, and in front of her is a massive and thick door. Four keys sit in the door's four keyholes, allowing it to have been opened.

Without the path clear, there's nothing to stop sound from traveling down the hall. If Atie had ears, she'd hear his heartbeat perfectly clear.
**End Chapter 10.1**

The world reforms. Alonsa marches through the desert, as a harsh wind rushes over the hills. Her black cloak billows through the air, the golden jewelry adorning it sparkling in the sunlight. Several other pilgrims march alongside her, all dressed in the same attire.
Alonsa looks at her hands
Her hands hold their familiar shape, wrapped in a black glove.
Her hands ache, with a familiar pain.
She grips them tightly, and walks forward at a faster pace

The man at the front of the pilgrimage holds out a hand towards her. Around his neck hangs a golden cross, denoting him of a higher rank.

"#$%@&, is there something the matter? It is best to conserve our energy until we reach the holy site."
“No, Father. Everything is well. Don’t worry.”
“How far are we?”
"It shouldn't be long now. If our information is accurate, the church will be rather easy to spot from a distance."
“Of course.”

The group continues forward through the arid sands. Eventually, a tower comes into view in the distance. A sandstone church, rising over a hundred meters into the sky, towering over the rather mundane town beneath it.
An oasis, in the middle of the desert. She continues toward it.

"Intriguing. Its height has significantly diminished since our latest records were taken." The leader stares at the tower, as he walks with Alonsa. "I suppose it must have sunk into the sand. Perhaps the Reaper has played a foul trick... or perhaps, with its prior tenant having abandoned it, the Prince's blessing has disappeared, leaving it to sink under its own weight."
"Do you think it will still be here, in ten thousand years?"
"At this rate, it's unlikely. We have much to do to ensure its preservation. Losing such a treasure would be unforgivable. Future generations would have no idea of its magnificence."
"Then we have a lot of work to do..."

"Yes." As the pilgrims approach the sparse buildings lying at the foot of the church, the leader points Alonsa towards the lone carriage at the back of group. "Retrieve our luggage. We may need to barter with the local authority."
She heads over promptly

She finds several items stored there. Food, currency, religious trinkets, and personal belongings. She knows what her superior was referring to, though. Two items sit in the carriage, wrapped in blankets. They were freshly created for this pilgrimage.
She unwraps them, just to check that they made it intact

Two children stare at her. They can't be more than a few months old. Their deep orange eyes, yet to truly see the world, look over her curiously. One baby swaddled in black, one swaddled in white, matching the colorings of their hair.
She smiles at them.
and takes them into her arms.
The baby in black silently accepts this, while the baby in white begins to cry.
She holds him tightly, but is silent towards him. She refuses to allow herself attachment.
Eventually, he calms down. Tired from the journey, he's lost the energy to resist.
Haven't we all
She walks with the children to the Father

He nods in approval, and approaches the town. There, a blond man with a rather rough-looking face is speaking to a young girl. He notices the approach of the piligrimage, and hands a knife to the girl.

"Looks like daddy's got some business to take care of. Go play with this for a bit." After he offers her these words, she runs off to another area of the village.
It’s an invitation, she thinks. He is telling us that he is unarmed. If he isn’t a fool, then he isnt really unarmed, and if he is wise, he knows that we know this.

The Father bows to the man. "Greetings. We are of the church of Panthium. We have come to your humble village in hopes of reinstating relations between this holy site and our capital church. We have the requisite manpower to run the institution, but we may require the assistance of the townsfolk in keeping our church properly stocked. I believe with a unified effort, we can return the Prince's blessing to-"

The man cuts him off. "I get it, I get it. You're lookin' to squat in my territory. Don't really care why, you religious nutjobs can shove your prayers up someone else's ass. Just tell me. Whaddaya got for me? Rent ain't free here."

The Father motions for Alonsa to step forward.
Alonsa shows him the offerings

He examines them carefully. "Hm... Mmm... Uh huh..." He nods. "Looks healthy enough... we could use a couple o' hands to help out... an' they're young enough to be moldable still... Alright, not bad, not bad. I'll take 'em off your hands, and help y'all set up shop."

The man holds out his hands, and the Father nods to Alonsa.
“Take care of them.”
“They’ll need it.”
He raises an eyebrow. "They're mine to do what I see fit with. Or is that gonna be a problem?"
“No.”
“Do what you will.”

He takes the children into his arms, and turns back to the Father. "I keep the key to the church behind the counter at the inn. Feel free to let yourself in. Gotta discuss assignments for your gifts with the sheriff." He motions towards the inn, and sets off towards the sheriff's office with his newly aquired property.
A cruel fate, but sacrifices are necessary. History is built on bones.
She heads into the inn.

The key's exactly where she was told it would be, and exactly where it will be untold years later. History proceeds undisturbed. A congratulations is in order, for the archeologist willing to preserve all that matters to her, and nothing else.
**End Chapter 100.4**
